key_insight: Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 double perovskites show composition-tunable self-trapped excitons: B-site alloying shifts emission color and polarization anisotropy while leaving the main absorption edge nearly unchanged.
engineering_relevance: These lead-free double perovskites offer a way to tune photoluminescence color and optical anisotropy through composition control, useful for optoelectronic and photocatalytic material design.
method: Optical spectroscopy on Na-to-K alloyed Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals
Ab initio calculations of excitonic states and lattice distortions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports PL tuning from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV with nearly constant absorption near 3.8 eV, and the measured anisotropy closely matches theory.
watch_item: Because the key optical response comes from strong exciton-phonon coupling and self-trapping, device performance may be sensitive to small composition or processing variations.
paper_title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
